newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu denies decision on Israel economic plan.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu denies decision on Israel economic plan.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's spokesman denied on Sunday a newspaper report the Israeli leader had decided on a comprehensive economic plan to revitalise the country's sluggish economy.

Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper said Netanyahu had reached a decision on a programme to widen the Israeli shekel's trading bands, liberalise foreign currency controls, set lower interest rate targets and enact further cuts in the 1997 budget.
"The prime minister has not yet decided on the issue. The details of this decision have not been finally set," the spokesman, Shai Bazak, said in a statement.
Finance Minister Dan Meridor called the newspaper report unfounded.
"Unfortunately, there is a currently an imbalance that prevents liberalisation of the foreign exchange market," Meridor told reporters.
He was apparently referring to high interest rates set by the central bank which have attracted an inflow of foreign capital and put pressure on the shekel exchange rate.
An economic programme had been under discussion for weeks but disagreements between Meridor, Netanyahu and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel had prevented any decision.
The report said Netanyahu had stepped in to break the deadlock.
"There is no difference of opinion over liberalisation. The aim has been agreed upon...the question is the timetable," Meridor said.
